capabilities: Sync a vault across devices through a self-hosted server
Encrypt note contents, attachments, and configuration end-to-end so the server cannot read them
Manage multiple users, each with an access key and separate vaults
Resolve conflicting edits by selecting, keeping both, merging, or postponing
Exclude files per device by size, folder, extension, or regular expression
extras: The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff. The README warns users to back up their vault before first use, states there is no version-history or recycle-bin interface, and lists pending work: Android credential-storage integration, continuous background sync, and SQLite server support.
problem: Obsidian's built-in Sync is a paid service, so users who want to sync through their own server with end-to-end encryption have no first-party option.

requires.name: user account with access key created in the server's admin page

summary: Self-hosted vault sync with end-to-end encryption, multi-user access keys, and conflict resolution.
